Four P0/P1 findings, all found by re-reading rather than by a failing test: (1) saispin_watch.ps1 Write-SaispinState used File.Copy, which TRUNCATES the destination and streams into it -- the exact half-written state file the atomic write exists to prevent, and a truncated state reads as a fresh history, silently resetting every streak; now File.Replace with a Move fallback for the first-ever write (Replace requires an existing target). (2) The engine extended a streak across an arbitrary gap, so a laptop that slept two days woke holding five strikes -- a kill from history nobody was observing; STALE_GAP_SECONDS now restarts the streak past 30min. (3) OutputEncoding is ASCII on Windows PowerShell 5.1: every non-ASCII process name/path crossed the pipe as question marks, and since the kill gate compares the decision name to the live one, such a process could be detected forever but never acted on; pipes pinned to UTF-8, and the global scope modifier is load-bearing -- a local assignment silently changes nothing. (4) Kill gate hardened with allowlist/PID<=4/name-change refusals before Stop-Process. Re-ran the ticket verify independently: test_saispin 52 checks, watcher -SelfTest 35 checks incl. 2 new state-swap and 1 Unicode round-trip check, 0 failures on BOTH 5.1 and pwsh 7; live dry-run 312-314 processes, streak accumulated 1->2 across sweeps, no .tmp debris; test_regs + test_limits green; installer -WhatIf clean

There is no editable client source to patch: bin/ holds the binary, node_modules two per-arch binary packages. Discovery: the official @opencode-ai/plugin API (installed locally as a config dependency) exposes server plugins with an event(input) hook receiving every Event, including session.status and session.idle, and a chat.message hook that runs before a user message is accepted. The @opencode-ai/sdk exposes POST /session/id/message with agent/model/noReply/system/tools/parts, GET /session/id/status returning idle/retry/busy, and DELETE for abort. This decides the design: a server PLUGIN, not a binary patch -- it sits inside OpenCode own extension surface, survives upgrades that keep the hook contract, and is refused when the contract cannot be proved. Read the installed host: api.route is exactly route:{register, navigate, get current()} - there is NO route-change subscription, so the plugin cannot be told the foreground moved. selectionFromRoute derives the session from the host's own live route getter and syncSelectionFromRoute acts only when that value actually changes. It runs at init, immediately after a navigation issued through api.route.navigate (ownership-aware wrapper that restores the prior function on dispose and never clobbers a newer owner), and on every native host event. Selection is NEVER inferred from an event sessionID, so background execution still cannot repaint the foreground. The honest liveness bound is documented: a navigation producing no subsequent host activity is not observed until the next one
